---
title: "Publications"
toc: false
bibliography: publications.bib
# APA is used over Quarto's Chicago default for two reasons: it renders titles in
# sentence case (Chicago title-cases them, which corrupts species epithets into
# "Drosophila Melanogaster") and it lists up to 20 authors instead of eliding to
# "et al." after three.
csl: assets/apa.csl
nocite: |
  @*
link-citations: true
---

My name is shown in bold. This list is generated from
[`publications.bib`](https://github.com/mkash006/mkash006.github.io/blob/main/publications.bib);
the same file is also on [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=BZ-46-8AAAAJ&hl=en).

::: {#refs}
:::

```{=html}
<script>
// The bibliography is generated by citeproc, so the author name can only be
// emphasized after the fact. Matches both "Mayank Kashyap" and the inverted
// "Kashyap, Mayank" that CSL uses for the first author of an entry.
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const refs = document.getElementById("refs");
  if (!refs) return;
  // APA initializes given names, so the rendered form is "Kashyap, M." rather
  // than the full name that appears in the .bib.
  const self = /(Kashyap,\s+M\.|Kashyap,\s+Mayank|Mayank\s+Kashyap)/g;
  const walker = document.createTreeWalker(refs, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
  const targets = [];
  while (walker.nextNode()) {
    if (self.test(walker.currentNode.nodeValue)) targets.push(walker.currentNode);
    self.lastIndex = 0;
  }
  targets.forEach(function (node) {
    const span = document.createElement("span");
    span.innerHTML = node.nodeValue.replace(self, "<strong>$1</strong>");
    node.parentNode.replaceChild(span, node);
  });
});
</script>
```
